title: ethan-ross-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-09
content:
Daily scratchpad - Private deployment (Customer A)

Date: 2026-03-09
Owner: Ethan Ross
Context: Onboarding Customer A for on-prem/VPC deployment. This is a working list of install steps, reminders, and blockers from today's calls and lab runs. Not tidy — use linked Confluence page for customer-facing notes.

Objectives for this week:
- Complete network review + firewall rules with infra team
- Validate container runtime and GPU drivers on 4 target nodes
- Finish KMS/HSM integration smoke test
- Get final signed SLA and schedule weekend deployment window

Environment notes (Customer A):
- VPC CIDR: 10.140.0.0/16 (customer)
- Public egress via NAT Gateway in AZ-a (10.140.1.0/24)
- Bastion host: 10.140.1.12 (jump user: ops-bastion)
- Admin VPN: wireguard at vpn.customer-a.example.com
- KMS: AWS CloudHSM (managed) in us-east-1 (must confirm key policy)
- On-prem cluster runs RHEL 8.8, SELinux enforcing, firewalld enabled
- Nodes: 4 nodes (g5.2xlarge equiv), GPU: A10G, docker runtime=containerd

Quick install checklist (in progress):
[ ] Preflight: customer provided AR/VR of network topology (got diagrams 2026-03-08)
[ ] Confirmed SSH keys and jump host access (blocked: Ops waiting for customer firewall rule)
[ ] Update kernel + install NVidia driver (tested on lab node)
[ ] Install containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit config
[ ] Pull Redwood runtime image (private registry auth)
[ ] Run validation job: small model load, 1 concurrent session -> verify latency
[ ] KMS integration smoke test with sample secret -> success expected
[ ] Configure systemd unit + autorestart for runtime

Commands and notes run today:
- Kernel/driver:
  sudo yum update -y && sudo reboot (kernel bumped to 5.14.0-162)
  # After reboot install drivers:
  sudo yum localinstall -y NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-525.78.01.run
  nvidia-smi -> shows 0/4 GPUs on lab-node-03, driver 525.x OK

- container runtime:
  sudo yum install -y yum-utils device-mapper-persistent-data lvm2
  sudo yum-config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  sudo yum install -y containerd.io
  # configure /etc/containerd/config.toml -> ensure nvidia runtime containerd config present

- nvidia-container-toolkit:
  sudo distribution=$(. /etc/os-release;echo $ID$VERSION_ID)
  curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.repo | sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-docker.repo
  sudo yum install -y nvidia-docker2
  sudo systemctl restart containerd

Blockers / open items:
- CUSTOMER FIREWALL: Need ingress 10.140.1.12 -> our CI IPs (35.199.20.45 / 35.199.20.46). Ops emailed customer netsec; waiting on rule creation (JIRA-PL-849).
- KMS POLICY: CloudHSM team needs to add Redwood platform principal to key policy. Confluence page shows policy diff; awaiting final approval from customer security.
- SELinux: some of our container mounts hit denials (AVC). Quick workaround: setenforce Permissive for testing; long term need proper SELinux policy or use dedicated mount options. Note to self: capture audit2allow snippets.
- System time skew on node-02 (chrony drift ~12s). KMS signing fails intermittently until timesync is fixed. Plan: enable chronyd service & force sync, add NTP pool config.

Testing results (lab):
- Model load test (small-7B) -> success on node-03 with 1 session, p50 latency 180ms.
- Multi-session stress (4 concurrent) -> OOM on node-01 (GPU memory fragmentation). Hypothesis: CUDA drivers older on node-01; need driver reprovision.
- Persistent storage: tested NFS mount for /var/redwood/cache; mount options recommended: noatime,nodiratime,async. Observed occasional write latency spikes (~200ms) under load — consider local NVMe cache.

Customer reminders (from call 2026-03-09):
- Customer wants all admin ops through bastion only; no direct node public IPs
- Compliance requires audit logs retained 1 year; ask finance for cost estimate for S3 Glacier retention add-on
- Encryption at rest: customer will provide KMS key; we must not create keys in their account

Next steps (short):
- Follow up with netsec on firewall rules (today EOD) -> assign to Riley
- Re-provision node-01 driver (swap to 525.78.01) -> Maya to run tomorrow AM
- Create SELinux audit -> generate audit2allow patch and circulate to customer sec
- Re-run KMS smoke test after time sync fix
- Schedule weekend maintenance window (proposed: 2026-03-14 22:00-02:00 UTC)

Notes / loose thoughts:
- Could support a lighter install for customers who don't want HSM: soft-HSM with customer-managed keys? Need product input — tag product-ops.
- Consider packaging a one-click preflight script that collects kernel, nvidia, containerd, and SELinux status -> reduce onboarding friction. Might be a small RFC.

Reference links and tickets:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/12345/Customer+A+onboarding
- JIRA: JIRA-PL-849 (customer firewall)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/56 (installer: add chrony config)

End of scratchpad.

(Will clean up and copy to customer-facing doc once blockers resolved.)
